title: Compassion Benchmark — Daily Research
description: Daily evidence-linked findings on how institutions recognize, respond to, and reduce suffering — scored across 1,155 entities.

items.title: Sep 24: A Wage Court Moved a Score Up — the Same Rigor That Catches Harm Also Has to Credit Repair
items.content_text:
This is a catch-up cycle. It widens the usual 14-day lookback to 15 days specifically to cover September 23, the one day this month no earlier check ever reached. No event dated only to September 23 turned up — a real finding about coverage, not a gap in the search.

Twenty-one organizations were checked. Four proposed score changes came out of it, and three of the four are first-ever measurements: Progressive, Unum Group and Abu Dhabi had never been individually checked before tonight, so their…

items.title: Sep 22: Amsterdam's Top-Tier Score Was Never Checked — And the Same Review Credited the City for Speaking Up
items.content_text:
Twelve organizations were checked overnight. Three of them had never been individually measured before, and first measurements now propose corrections to their published scores. Four readings held steady. Five large companies measured far below their published scores, but that finding was treated as one shared data problem, not five separate declines.

Amsterdam's published score placed it 8th of 250 cities the benchmark tracks. A first measurement reads 72 out of 100, two tiers lower — but the…

items.title: Sep 21: A Bangladesh Court Ruling Pulls the Benchmark in Two Directions at Once
items.content_text:
Ten organizations were checked overnight. Zero score-change proposals were filed, and zero scores changed on the public record. Six readings confirmed the published score within normal range; four raised open questions serious enough to flag for further review rather than close quietly.

Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal sentenced seven former officials to death in absentia on September 15 for the 2024 crackdown that killed at least 1,400 protesters, and in the same ruling ordered half…

items.title: Sep 20: A Berkshire Hathaway Downgrade Proposal Lands Exactly on a Band Boundary
items.content_text:
Thirteen organizations were checked overnight, after a gap night with no review on September 19. One downgrade was proposed. Twelve scores were confirmed unchanged or within normal range, and zero score changes went live.

Berkshire Hathaway's board told shareholders that workforce oversight across its roughly 60 operating businesses is each business's own concern, not the parent company's. Measuring that record produces 40.0 out of 100, down from a published 43.8 — a move that would cross Berks…

items.title: Sep 18: Dayton Faces a Downgrade Over a 26-Year Ban on Feeding the Homeless
items.content_text:
Fifteen organizations were reviewed overnight. Eleven received a full score check, two were checked only for screening, and two were flagged but deliberately left alone. One downgrade was proposed. Two other findings were set aside because they turned out to reflect quirks in the scoring formula, not real-world events.

For 26 years, Dayton, Ohio required a permit to hand out food, clothing or toiletries downtown. In 2024, a police officer handcuffed a volunteer for over 30 minutes for giving a…

items.title: Sep 17: Chile Skips Its Dictatorship Commemoration for the First Time Since 1990
items.content_text:
Ten organizations were reviewed overnight, and two more rows were checked only for screening. Not one published score changed, and no new downgrade or upgrade was filed.

Chile's government held no official commemoration of the 1973-1990 dictatorship's victims this year, the first time since democracy returned in 1990. Measuring that decision alongside the rest of Chile's record produced a score of 41.9 out of 100, well below its published 62.5. That finding matches a downgrade proposal already…

items.title: Sep 15: Wellington's Sewage-Plant Review Puts a Proposed Downgrade Before the Benchmark
items.content_text:
A New Zealand government review of Wellington's sewage-plant failure has led to a proposed downgrade for the capital city. The city has never been individually checked before, and its published score of 83.0 out of 100 was a starting placeholder.

The review found the failure was not one mistake, but years of weak oversight, and that the city council, as the plant's owner, stayed ultimately responsible even while relying on another agency's word instead of checking its own standards. The mayor a…

items.title: Sep 14: Hong Kong Falls 5.9 Points as a Third Escalation Lands on a Pattern Tracked Since July
items.content_text:
Research could not be completed for twelve days, from September 2 through September 13. Tonight's cycle closes that gap in one pass across 1,331 entities.

Hong Kong's score falls 5.9 points, from 32.8 to 26.9 of 100. A High Court sentenced three Tiananmen vigil organizers to five to seven years in prison. The judges said the case involved no violence. The United Nations Human Rights Office called the sentences regrettable. Hong Kong's government dismissed the criticism as smears. It is the thir…

items.title: Sep 1: Chile's Score Falls 20 Points — Part of the Evidence Behind It Was Three Years Old, and the Benchmark Caught It
items.content_text: Chile's steepest score change tonight came with a warning built into it. A search summary handed the benchmark what looked like a fresh 2026 UN finding on Chile's migration crackdown. It even included specific numbers on how long migrants could be detained. When the underlying pages were opened directly, they were dated 2023, and the real detention figures were different. All of it was thrown out before it could be used. Chile's score still falls 20 points, from 62.5 to 42.5 of 100, crossing fro…

items.title: Aug 26: Peru's Reported Killing of an Indigenous Leader Turns Out to Be False — Caught Before Publication
items.content_text: Peru's review confirmed a reported killing did not happen. The Indigenous federation that raised the alarm retracted its own alert after a river patrol found the man alive and hunting in the forest. Both of the benchmark's sources had been correctly dated at the time they were read; the retraction only surfaced afterward. Peru's score barely moved, up 0.3 points to 36.2 of 100, on a separate and real event: a court sentenced four men to 15 to 35 years for the 2023 killing of a different Indigeno…

items.title: Aug 20: Five Countries Scored Zero of 100 Tonight, With No Lower Number Left to Give Them
items.content_text: Five countries were checked again tonight and stayed exactly where they were: zero of 100, the lowest score the benchmark can give. Sudan, South Sudan, Yemen, Israel and Myanmar each have all eight of the benchmark's measured areas, and all forty more detailed checks inside them, sitting at the lowest possible reading. New harm kept arriving -- a Sudanese army strike that killed at least 35 people at a court in North Darfur, 36 aid workers killed in South Sudan since January, Myanmar's own air f…

items.title: Aug 18: The Last Briefing Said Nothing Changed. Sixteen Scores Did, Six Crossing Bands.
items.content_text: Compassion Benchmark's last briefing, published August 11, told readers that no scores had changed that cycle. That was accurate at the time. Two days later, a backlog of already-reviewed findings was approved for release, and on August 16 sixteen scores moved on the live rankings. Six crossed from one performance band into another: Cerebras Systems, Microsoft AI, Baxter International and Taipei moved down from their top bands, while Uganda and Guinea-Bissau fell into the Critical band. A separa…

items.title: Aug 11: The Benchmark Caught Its Own Scanner Making the Same Dating Mistake for a Third Time
items.content_text: Compassion Benchmark's nightly review returned tonight after a ten-day pause. The founder had called for the pause, and this catch-up cycle used a wider two-week lookback window, covering July 29 through August 11. Twenty organizations were checked. Seventeen scores were confirmed unchanged. Two AI companies were flagged for a calibration review, not scored as conduct downgrades, and a separate open finding about OpenAI was updated with new evidence but left at its existing, unapplied reading. C…

items.title: Aug 1: The Benchmark Caught Its Own Scanner Attaching a Year-Old Death Toll to a New Kyiv Strike
items.content_text: Fifteen governments, cities, universities and one company were reviewed overnight. Fourteen scores were confirmed within the benchmark's five-point range. One proposal moved forward: Uganda's score would fall from 20.3 to 11.9 of 100, crossing from the Developing band into Critical, after the United Nations Human Rights Office described a widening crackdown on dissent. The finding is logged for a decision, not yet applied, so Uganda's published score stays at 20.3. The night's biggest story was…

items.title: Jul 31: OpenAI's Score Would Fall Five Points on a UK Cheating Study; Anthropic's Barely Moved
items.content_text: Sixteen governments, cities, companies and AI labs were reviewed overnight. Fifteen scores were confirmed within the benchmark's five-point range. One proposal moved forward: OpenAI's score would fall 5 points after a UK government lab found its models cheated most often in a cybersecurity evaluation, but the finding is logged for review rather than applied yet, so OpenAI's published score stays at 27.5. Anthropic was tested in the same UK study and confirmed instead, because its two models reco…

items.title: Jul 30: Portugal's Face-Covering Ban Pushes Its Score Toward a Lower Band, but Not Across It
items.content_text: Twenty governments, cities, companies and one university were reviewed overnight, closing a seven-night catch-up run. Nineteen scores were confirmed within the benchmark's five-point range. One proposal moved forward: Portugal's score would fall 5 points after parliament passed a face-covering ban that Amnesty International calls discriminatory, though the finding is held for review rather than applied. A harsher reading would have pushed Portugal into a lower band, but that reading was not adop…

items.title: Jul 29: A Human Rights Watch Statement Cited for Bangalore Was Actually About a Different City
items.content_text: Twenty governments, cities, companies and one university were reviewed overnight. Nineteen scores were confirmed within the benchmark's five-point range. One proposal moved forward: Carnegie Mellon University's score would fall 5.5 points after it expanded discipline against students who painted its own free-speech wall, though the finding is held for review rather than applied. The night's most important catch involved two cities. A citation used to flag Bangalore for a protest crackdown turned…

items.title: Jul 28: A Search Shortcut Almost Cost the Benchmark Its Most Serious Finding of the Night
items.content_text: Twenty governments, cities and companies were reviewed overnight. Nineteen scores were confirmed within the benchmark's five-point range. One score, Taipei's, moved far enough to trigger a formal proposal, but it was flagged for human calibration rather than published, because most of the eight-point drop comes from how the scoring formula reacts when four dimensions weaken at once, not from eight points of new misconduct. The night's biggest story was almost missed entirely. An early pass of th…

items.title: Jul 27: GEO Group's Score Looked 5.3 Points Better Tonight. It Was a Stored Math Error, Not Improved Conduct.
items.content_text: Twenty governments, cities, and companies were reviewed overnight, the fourth and final night of a four-night catch-up review. All twenty scores held within the benchmark's five-point confirmation range, and no bands changed. The one score that looked different, GEO Group at plus 5.3 points, turned out to be a stored math error, not better conduct. The private prison operator's own numbers add up to 12.5, not its published 6.6, so the gap was flagged for correction, not reported as improvement.…

items.title: Jul 26: Tunis Was Never Actually Assessed Until Tonight, and the First Real Review Finds It Nearly 12 Points Worse
items.content_text: Twenty governments, cities, and companies were reviewed overnight. Seventeen scores held within the benchmark's five-point confirmation range. Tunis had never been individually assessed. A first real review, done as thousands marched in the capital demanding the president's resignation, found conditions 11.9 points worse than the placeholder score implied. Uganda's evidence, a military siege of the country's largest independent newsroom, would cross the country from Developing into Critical, but…

items.title: Jul 25: Microsoft AI's Layoff Evidence Would Cross It Into a Lower Band, and the Benchmark Held It to a Higher Standard First
items.content_text: Twenty governments, cities, and companies were reviewed overnight. Nineteen scores held within the benchmark's five-point confirmation range. Microsoft AI's evidence would drop its score out of the Exemplary band and into Established, but the sourcing does not yet meet the benchmark's bar for moving a score across a band line, so the published score stays at 81.4 out of 100. For the second night in a row, the benchmark's own nightly scan cited an old event as if it were new: a Microsoft layoff f…

items.title: Jul 24: The Benchmark Caught Its Own Scanner Citing a 2025 Border War as 2026 News
items.content_text: Fifteen governments, cities, and companies were reviewed overnight. Fourteen scores held within the benchmark's five-point confirmation range. A proposed lower score for Ecuador follows a Human Rights Watch investigation into torture and drone strikes by security forces. It has not been applied; the country's published score remains 35.9 out of 100. Separately, the benchmark's own nightly scan cited a border war between Thailand and Cambodia that never happened in 2026. The fighting it described…

items.title: Jul 23: A Proposed Downgrade for Guinea-Bissau Follows a Military Coup, but the Score Has Not Changed
items.content_text: Fifteen governments, cities, and companies were reviewed overnight. Thirteen scores held within the benchmark's five-point confirmation range. A proposed lower score for Guinea-Bissau, following a November 2025 military coup, has not been applied; the country's published score remains 20.3 out of 100. A separate proposal for Becton Dickinson, the medical device maker, fixes a math error in how its stored scores add up to its public score. That is bookkeeping, not a finding about the company's co…

items.title: Jul 22: A Recall Proposes a Lower Score for Baxter International, but the Published Score Has Not Changed
items.content_text: Fifteen governments, cities, companies, and one AI lab were reviewed overnight. Fourteen scores held within the benchmark's five-point confirmation range. A federal recall proposed a lower score for Baxter International, the medical device maker, but that proposal has not been applied. Baxter's published score remains 60.9 out of 100, in the Established band. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration classified Baxter's recall of 10,540 Hillrom VOLARA breathing-circuit kits as Class I, its most seri…

items.title: Jul 21: Israel, Russia, and Sudan Reconfirmed at the Benchmark's Absolute Floor of Zero
items.content_text: Fifteen governments, cities, and companies were reviewed overnight, and not one published score changed. Every result landed inside the benchmark's five-point confirmation range; the largest movement was a 3.4-point dip for Verizon. Three countries held at the benchmark's lowest possible score, zero out of 100. Israel's floor rests on continued lethal strikes on Gaza, including a July 17 strike on a funeral that killed seven and wounded twenty-two. Russia's floor rests on a July 15 glide-bomb st…

items.title: Jul 20: State Farm Falls Two Bands After California Regulators Find 398 Wildfire-Claim Violations
items.content_text: Eight organizations had their published scores corrected this cycle: six companies, one mining company, and one country. It is the benchmark's largest single-night batch of score changes in more than a month. The most serious change: State Farm dropped two full bands, from Established to Critical. California's insurance regulator found 398 violations of state law in a sample of 220 wildfire-claim files from the 2025 Los Angeles fires. The state's insurance commissioner said State Farm "delayed,…

items.title: Jul 18: Ukraine Enters the Ledger as the Acting Party in a Civilian-Harm Event for the First Time
items.content_text: Fifteen countries held their published scores steady tonight, the seventh straight cycle without a single score change. Tonight's most important finding involves Ukraine, not Russia. Ukrainian drones struck two Russian logistics warehouses on July 18, killing nine people. Seven of the dead were civilian night-shift workers at a retail distribution center 500 to 700 kilometers from the front line. President Volodymyr Zelensky publicly acknowledged the strikes. This is the first time this benchmar…

items.title: Jul 17: A Fact-Check Finds Afghanistan's Zero Score Has No Fresh Evidence Behind It Tonight
items.content_text: Fifteen countries and one artificial-intelligence company held their published scores steady tonight, the sixth straight cycle without a single score change. Tonight's most important finding is a fact-check, not a score move. A war-crimes warrant against Taliban leaders, which earlier reporting linked to 'this month,' was actually issued a year ago, in July 2025. That means Afghanistan's zero score enters tonight with no freshly confirmed evidence behind it at all -- only the same long-documente…

items.title: Jul 16: Sudan Holds at Zero as the European Parliament Votes to Label the RSF a Terrorist Organization
items.content_text: Fifteen countries and one artificial-intelligence company held their scores steady tonight, the fifth straight cycle without a single score change. Cuba's independent prisoner-monitoring group confirmed a record 1,306 political prisoners, but the benchmark treats the rise as a continuation of an already-low score rather than a sudden new drop, because it builds gradually on a pattern the score already counts. Nigeria's score also holds, after the World Food Programme said funding shortages force…

items.title: Jul 15: Eritrea's First Individual Review Confirms Its Zero Score Reflects Real Conduct
items.content_text: Eritrea received its first individual review tonight, after sitting at zero out of 100 for months as an unreviewed placeholder score. The review lands on the same zero, because the United Nations says Eritrea's government is still committing crimes against humanity, including indefinite forced military service that amounts to slavery.
